title: Wearable biomedical systems: signal acquisition, processing and clinical translation

record.title: Wearable biomedical systems: signal acquisition, processing and clinical translation
record.abstract: This book chapter provides a comprehensive overview of the engineering challenges involved in translating wearable biomedical sensing systems from laboratory prototypes to clinically validated devices. The chapter covers the full signal chain from electrode–skin interface physics and analog front-end design through digital signal processing pipelines to clinical validation methodology. Particular attention is paid to the interplay between hardware constraints—power budget, memory, communication bandwidth—and algorithm design choices for cardiac and motion signals. The ECG acquisition and arrhythmia detection pipeline is used as a running example throughout, illustrating how design decisions at each layer propagate to end-to-end system performance. A dedicated section addresses regulatory considerations under the European Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) relevant to software-as-a-medical-device classification of on-device diagnostic algorithms. The chapter concludes with a roadmap for future research directions including personalized adaptive algorithms, multi-sensor fusion, and privacy-preserving distributed learning. It is intended as a graduate-level reference for students and practitioners entering the field of wearable medical technology.
